I have been farming these 13.5 mu for many years, so I know what works on my land. Here is how I will split it this year, same as before:

**Cotton — 8 mu.** Cotton is my main crop, the soil here is a bit salty so cotton handles it better than grain. I will use improved Bt seed like I did last year — bollworm is much less trouble with it. I plough the field before planting. I apply about 15 kg urea plus one bag (50 kg) of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu as base, then topdress another 10 kg urea at flowering. That works out to around 17 kg N, 8 kg P, 8 kg K per mu. I water 3 times — before planting, at bud stage, at flowering. Cotton pests are many, so I spray 6-7 times against aphids, mites, bollworm. Normal year I get around 260 kg seed cotton per mu.

**Wheat — 5.5 mu (winter).** I sow improved variety in October. Plough and rotary before sowing. Base fertilizer one bag compound (50 kg) plus 10 kg urea per mu, topdress 10 kg urea at jointing. Around 15 kg N, 8 kg P, 7 kg K. Water 3 times — before winter, jointing, filling. Spray 2 times for aphids and rust. Yield about 470 kg.

**Maize — 5.5 mu (summer, after wheat).** No-till sow right after wheat harvest to save time and moisture. Improved hybrid seed. Fertilizer 40 kg compound at sowing plus 15 kg urea topdress at big trumpet stage — about 16 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Water 2 times if no rain. Spray 2 times for corn borer and armyworm. About 520 kg per mu.

I don't change much from year to year. My neighbors do about the same. Fertilizer is expensive but cutting it costs me more in yield.
